evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A02031-003 研訂說明; historical entries and variant relation
evidence.text: The dictionary treats 机 and 機 as distinct entries found in Shuowen: 机 is glossed 木也 and analyzed 从木几聲, while 機 is glossed 主發謂之機 and analyzed 从木幾聲. It reports different fanqie readings (机 居履切; 機 居依切), says later writers often borrowed 机 for 機 because of their similar sound, and notes that this long-established usage became the simplified form in mainland China. The entry lists later witnesses including Song–Yuan popular-script collections and the mainland simplified-character table. This supports 机 as a borrowed graphic substitute/simplified form for 機, not a chronological ancestor of 機.
evidence.title: [A02031-003] 机 (機) - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, Shuowen entry and Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: The entry gives 機 as 主發謂之機 and analyzes it 从木幾聲. Duan Yucai explains that the loom mechanism is named for its function of initiating/releasing action, and extends the term to things that initiate or trigger. The page gives the reading fanqie 居衣切. This is a historical lexicographic account, not direct evidence for the graph’s earliest physical form.
evidence.title: 說文解字「機」 - Shuowen.org

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.field: 機 entry: Shuowen, gloss and historical usage discussion
evidence.text: The database reports 木 as semantic classifier and 幾 as phonetic component; it interprets the original sense as the trigger/release mechanism of a crossbow. It cites 尚書·太甲上 若虞機張 and 呂氏春秋·察微 夫弩機差以米則不發 as early textual examples; it then documents broader senses including mechanisms, loom, crucial point, secrecy, opportunity, innate disposition, and ingenuity, with examples attributed to early classics and later historical works. These are reported textual examples; the webpage does not establish the manuscript date of each wording, and old text chronology should not be read directly from this gloss sequence.
evidence.kind: dictionary account with cited textual examples
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 機

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.field: 機 entry: phonology and component account
evidence.text: The database records 機 as jī in modern Mandarin, gives Guangyun fanqie 居依 and Middle Chinese category 見, level tone, 止攝微韻, open division III. Its historical account explicitly assigns 木 the semantic role and 幾 the phonetic role. The component account does not establish 幾’s earliest depicted referent; that uncertainty does not itself negate the independently stated phonetic role.

evidence.field: A00319-002 机 (几), documentary references and sound distinctions
evidence.text: The dictionary catalogues 机 as a variant under 几, cites 隸辨 quoting the 州輔碑, and records the Shuowen witness under 几部. It also indexes historical dictionary and inscription collections, though many image resources are unavailable on the inspected page. This supports the long documentary existence of the 机 graph separately from its later use for 機, while a dated earliest inscriptional occurrence and original tree referent remain unverified here.

The chapter belongs to 呂氏春秋, compiled in the late Warring States period (traditionally completed 241 BCE), though this textual witness alone is not a dated manuscript attestation.

gaps: No reliable, visually inspected oracle-bone or bronze forms for either graph were verified. The inspected CUHK paleographic catalog shows a small-seal form for 機 but no displayed oracle-bone/bronze form; lack of display is not evidence of absence.
The precise early graphic development from ancient forms to seal script and clerical/regular forms, including any graphic corruption hypothesis, remains unestablished by inspected evidence.
The historic tree referent and its spoken name for the original 机 are not independently recovered. A reconstruction of 机’s character reading does not prove a particular ancient tree name.
The MOE account supports later borrowing of 机 for 機 and modern simplification, but the exact first dated occurrence of 机 used for 機 was not established; only later source traditions are identified.

Modern readings recorded in the dossier include Mandarin jī for both graphs. The externally inspected CUHK page independently gives 機 jī; its accessible 机 page was not retrieved, while MOE gives distinct historical fanqie categories and distinguishes jī/jǐ scopes. Japanese kun/on readings in the dossier were not independently researched because the evidence pertains to Chinese graphic history.

Baxter–Sagart local rows were checked exactly: row 1457 机 *krəjʔ and row 1460 機 *kəj. The upstream PDF direct-open attempt failed; its search result confirms 機 *kəj but not 机, so the local-file reading cannot be represented as fully upstream-verified external evidence.

The early senses and later extensions are separately reported from lexicographic accounts and cited texts. The received-text examples do not establish the date of the physical manuscript or prove a linear semantic chronology.

The inspected sources here do not independently establish oracle-bone or bronze forms or a graphic corruption sequence for 机/機. The chosen illustration is explicitly a modern redraw of a seal-script form, not a photograph or facsimile of an ancient artifact.

The old name and pronunciation of the tree sense associated with 机 are not independently recovered. A reconstruction of the character reading cannot by itself prove that tree-name pronunciation, so this research does not establish the sound basis for any proposed whole-graph loan from the tree word.

This run did not independently inspect earliest semantic attestations or the sequence of semantic extensions; the prior dossier’s account of received-text examples and its manuscript-date caveat remains the relevant limitation.
The exact Baxter–Sagart rows are identified in the local dataset, but upstream PDF access was not obtained in this run; local notation is therefore not external verification.
